name_translation: The Yoga of the Supreme Person

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ऊर्ध्वमूलमधःशाखमश्वत्थं प्राहुरव्ययम् |
छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित् || १ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ऊर्ध्वमूलमधःशाखमश्वत्थं प्राहुरव्ययम् |
छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित् || १ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
ūrdhvamūlamadhaḥśākhamaśvatthaṃ prāhuravyayam |
chandāṃsi yasya parṇāni yastaṃ veda sa vedavit || 1 ||
verses.word_meanings: śrī-bhagavān uvāca—the Supreme Lord said; ūrdhva-mūlam—with roots above (in Brahman); adhaḥ-śākham—with branches below (in material realms); aśvattham—the sacred banyan/Ashvattha tree of cosmic existence; prāhuḥ—they declare; avyayam—eternal/imperishable; chandāṃsi—the Vedic hymns; yasya—of which; parṇāni—the leaves; yaḥ—whoever; tam—that; veda—knows; saḥ—he; veda-vit—the knower of the Vedas.
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord said: They speak of an imperishable Ashvattha tree with its roots above in Brahman and branches below in the cosmos, whose leaves are the Vedic hymns. He who understands this cosmic tree is truly a knower of the Vedas.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna employs the Vedic allegory of the inverted Ashvattha tree (Katha Upanishad 2.3.1) to symbolize the material universe (Samsara). Its ultimate root is 'Urdhva'—the transcendent Parabrahman; its branches spread downward as myriad species, planets, and mental states; and the ritualistic Vedic hymns are its protective leaves. Knowing the mechanics of this cosmic tree enables the seeker to transcend it.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna employs the Vedic allegory of the inverted Ashvattha tree (Katha Upanishad 2.3.1) to symbolize the material universe (Samsara). Its ultimate root is 'Urdhva'—the transcendent Parabrahman; its branches spread downward as myriad species, planets, and mental states; and the ritualistic Vedic hymns are its protective leaves. Knowing the mechanics of this cosmic tree enables the seeker to transcend it.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अधश्चोर्ध्वं प्रसृतास्तस्य शाखा गुणप्रवृद्धा विषयप्रवालाः |
अधश्च मूलान्यनुसन्ततानि कर्मानुबन्धीनि मनुष्यलोके || २ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अधश्चोर्ध्वं प्रसृतास्तस्य शाखा गुणप्रवृद्धा विषयप्रवालाः |
अधश्च मूलान्यनुसन्ततानि कर्मानुबन्धीनि मनुष्यलोके || २ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
adhaścordhvaṃ prasṛtāstasya śākhā guṇapravṛddhā viṣayapravālāḥ |
adhaśca mūlānyanusantatāni karmānubandhīni manuṣyaloke || 2 ||
verses.word_meanings: adhaḥ ca—downward; ūrdhvam—upward; prasṛtāḥ—spread out; tasya—its; śākhāḥ—branches; guṇa-pravṛddhāḥ—nourished by the three gunas; viṣaya-pravālāḥ—with sense objects as tender buds/shoots; adhaḥ ca—and downward; mūlāni—the secondary roots; anusantatāni—extended/ramified; karma-anubandhīni—binding to action; manuṣya-loke—in the world of human beings.
verses.translation: Its branches spread both downwards and upwards, nourished by the three gunas, with sense objects as its tender buds; and its secondary roots stretch downwards into the human realm, binding souls fast according to their karmic actions.
verses.meaning: The branches extend upward into celestial planes and downward into sub-human realms, watered by Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas. The secondary roots represent latent psychological impressions (Samskaras) and desires (Vasanas) that sprout in the human realm, generating fresh karma that perpetuates embodiment.
verses.purport: The branches extend upward into celestial planes and downward into sub-human realms, watered by Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas. The secondary roots represent latent psychological impressions (Samskaras) and desires (Vasanas) that sprout in the human realm, generating fresh karma that perpetuates embodiment.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
न रूपमस्येह तथोपलभ्यते नान्तो न चादिर्न च सम्प्रतिष्ठा |
अश्वत्थमेनं सुविरूढमूलमसङ्गशस्त्रेण दृढेन छित्त्वा || ३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
न रूपमस्येह तथोपलभ्यते नान्तो न चादिर्न च सम्प्रतिष्ठा |
अश्वत्थमेनं सुविरूढमूलमसङ्गशस्त्रेण दृढेन छित्त्वा || ३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
na rūpamasyeha tathopalabhyate nānto na cādirna ca sampratiṣṭhā |
aśvatthamenaṃ suvirūḍhamūlamasaṅgaśastreṇa dṛḍhena chittvā || 3 ||
verses.word_meanings: na—not; rūpam—real form/nature; asya—of this tree; iha—here in this world; tathā—as such; upalabhyate—is perceived; na antaḥ—neither its end; na ca ādiḥ—nor its beginning; na ca sampratiṣṭhā—nor its true foundation; aśvattham enam—this Ashvattha tree; su-virūḍha-mūlam—whose roots are firmly anchored; asaṅga-śastreṇa—with the weapon of detachment; dṛḍhena—strong/unyielding; chittvā—having severed/felled.
verses.translation: Its real form is not perceived here in this world—neither its beginning, nor its end, nor its foundation. Having severed this deeply rooted Ashvattha tree with the formidable weapon of unyielding detachment (Asanga-shastra);
verses.meaning: Samsara is boundless and confusing when viewed from within. It has no discernible beginning or end for the embodied soul. The only way to achieve liberation is not to prune individual branches, but to cut down the entire tree of psychological clinging at its very base using the sharp axe of non-attachment (Asanga).
verses.purport: Samsara is boundless and confusing when viewed from within. It has no discernible beginning or end for the embodied soul. The only way to achieve liberation is not to prune individual branches, but to cut down the entire tree of psychological clinging at its very base using the sharp axe of non-attachment (Asanga).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ततः पदं तत्परिमार्गितव्यं यस्मिन्गता न निवर्तन्ति भूयः |
तमेव चाद्यं पुरुषं प्रपद्ये यतः प्रवृत्तिः प्रसृता पुराणी || ४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ततः पदं तत्परिमार्गितव्यं यस्मिन्गता न निवर्तन्ति भूयः |
तमेव चाद्यं पुरुषं प्रपद्ये यतः प्रवृत्तिः प्रसृता पुराणी || ४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
tataḥ padaṃ tatparimārgitavyaṃ yasmingatā na nivartanti bhūyaḥ |
tameva cādyaṃ puruṣaṃ prapadye yataḥ pravṛttiḥ prasṛtā purāṇī || 4 ||
verses.word_meanings: tataḥ—thereafter; padam tat—that supreme abode/state; parimārgitavyam—must be sought; yasmin—wherein; gatāḥ—having gone; na nivartanti—they do not return; bhūyaḥ—again; tam eva—unto Him alone; ca—and; ādyam puruṣam—the Primeval Supreme Person; prapadye—I surrender; yataḥ—whence; pravṛttiḥ—the cosmic manifestation/activity; prasṛtā—has streamed forth; purāṇī—ancient/beginningless.
verses.translation: Thereafter, that supreme state must be sought, reaching which one never returns again to mortal birth, resolving: 'I surrender unto that Primeval Supreme Person (Adya Purusha) from whom this ancient cosmic stream has expanded.'
verses.meaning: Detachment from worldly illusions is only the first step; it must be coupled with wholehearted surrender to the Primeval Lord (Prapatti). Seeking that supreme transcendental sanctuary ensures that the soul is never cast back into the cycle of birth and death.
verses.purport: Detachment from worldly illusions is only the first step; it must be coupled with wholehearted surrender to the Primeval Lord (Prapatti). Seeking that supreme transcendental sanctuary ensures that the soul is never cast back into the cycle of birth and death.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
निर्मानमोहा जितसङ्गदोषा अध्यात्मनित्या विनिवृत्तकामाः |
द्वन्द्वैर्विमुक्ताः सुखदुःखसञ्ज्ञैर्गच्छन्त्यमूढाः पदमव्ययं तत् || ५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
निर्मानमोहा जितसङ्गदोषा अध्यात्मनित्या विनिवृत्तकामाः |
द्वन्द्वैर्विमुक्ताः सुखदुःखसञ्ज्ञैर्गच्छन्त्यमूढाः पदमव्ययं तत् || ५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
nirmānamohā jitasaṅgadoṣā adhyātmanityā vinivṛttakāmāḥ |
dvandvairvimuktāḥ sukhaduḥkhasañjñairgacchantyamūḍhāḥ padamavyayaṃ tat || 5 ||
verses.word_meanings: nih-māna-mohāḥ—free from pride and delusion; jita-saṅga-doṣāḥ—victorious over the fault of attachment; adhyātma-nityāḥ—constantly established in self-knowledge; vinivṛtta-kāmāḥ—their desires completely subdued; dvandvaiḥ—from dualities; vimuktāḥ—liberated; sukha-duḥkha-sañjñaiḥ—known as pleasure and pain; gacchanti—attain; amūḍhāḥ—the undeluded sages; padam avyayam tat—that imperishable supreme abode.
verses.translation: Free from vanity and delusion, victorious over the fault of attachment, constantly established in self-knowledge, their desires completely subdued, liberated from the dualities of pleasure and pain—the undeluded sages attain that eternal, imperishable state.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna lists the cardinal qualifications of the liberated sage (Amudha): freedom from egoic prestige, eradication of false identification, mastery over desires, and unperturbed equanimity amidst dualities.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna lists the cardinal qualifications of the liberated sage (Amudha): freedom from egoic prestige, eradication of false identification, mastery over desires, and unperturbed equanimity amidst dualities.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
न तद्भासयते सूर्यो न शशाङ्को न पावकः |
यद्गत्वा न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम || ६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
न तद्भासयते सूर्यो न शशाङ्को न पावकः |
यद्गत्वा न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम || ६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
na tadbhāsayate sūryo na śaśāṅko na pāvakaḥ |
yadgatvā na nivartante taddhāma paramaṃ mama || 6 ||
verses.word_meanings: na—not; tat—that; bhāsayate—illuminates; sūryaḥ—the sun; na—nor; śaśāṅkaḥ—the moon; na—nor; pāvakaḥ—fire; yat—where; gatvā—having gone; na nivartante—they never return; tat—that; dhāma—abode; paramam—supreme; mama—My.
verses.translation: Neither the sun, nor the moon, nor fire illuminates That; having attained which souls never return to mortal bondage—that is My Supreme Abode (Paramam Dhama).
verses.meaning: This renowned Upanishadic verse (Katha Upanishad 2.2.15, Mundaka 2.2.10) reveals the nature of the transcendental realm (Paramam Dhama / Vaikuntha / Goloka). It is self-luminous pure Consciousness, requiring no external physical luminescence, and provides permanent liberation from the cycle of rebirth.
verses.purport: This renowned Upanishadic verse (Katha Upanishad 2.2.15, Mundaka 2.2.10) reveals the nature of the transcendental realm (Paramam Dhama / Vaikuntha / Goloka). It is self-luminous pure Consciousness, requiring no external physical luminescence, and provides permanent liberation from the cycle of rebirth.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ममैवांशो जीवलोके जीवभूतः सनातनः |
मनःषष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि प्रकृतिस्थानि कर्षति || ७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ममैवांशो जीवलोके जीवभूतः सनातनः |
मनःषष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि प्रकृतिस्थानि कर्षति || ७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
mamaivāṃśo jīvaloke jīvabhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ |
manaḥṣaṣṭhānīndriyāṇi prakṛtisthāni karṣati || 7 ||
verses.word_meanings: mama eva aṃśaḥ—an eternal fragment/spark of My very Self; jīva-loke—in the world of living beings; jīva-bhūtaḥ—becoming the embodied soul; sanātanaḥ—eternal; manaḥ-ṣaṣṭhāni—the six including the mind; indriyāṇi—the senses; prakṛti-sthāni—abiding in material nature; karṣati—draws / struggles with.
verses.translation: An eternal portion (Amsha) of My very Self, becoming the embodied soul (Jiva) in the world of living entities, draws unto itself the five senses and the mind as the sixth, which abide in material nature.
verses.meaning: This master verse defines the constitutional identity of every soul: The Jiva is not an accidental biological product, but an eternal, qualitative fragment (Sanatana Amsha) of the Supreme Divine. In the material sphere, it becomes entangled by dragging along the mind and senses through consecutive lives.
verses.purport: This master verse defines the constitutional identity of every soul: The Jiva is not an accidental biological product, but an eternal, qualitative fragment (Sanatana Amsha) of the Supreme Divine. In the material sphere, it becomes entangled by dragging along the mind and senses through consecutive lives.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
शरीरं यदवाप्नोति यच्चाप्युत्क्रामतीश्वरः |
गृहीत्वैतानि संयाति वायुर्गन्धानिवाशयात् || ८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
शरीरं यदवाप्नोति यच्चाप्युत्क्रामतीश्वरः |
गृहीत्वैतानि संयाति वायुर्गन्धानिवाशयात् || ८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
śarīraṃ yadavāpnoti yaccāpyutkrāmatīśvaraḥ |
gṛhītvaitāni saṃyāti vāyurgandhānivāśayāt || 8 ||
verses.word_meanings: śarīram—a physical body; yat—when; avāpnoti—obtains; yat ca api—and also when; utkrāmati—departs/leaves; īśvaraḥ—the master of the body (the Jiva); gṛhītvā—taking; etāni—these (senses and mind); saṃyāti—migrates/moves; vāyuḥ—the wind; gandhān—fragrances; iva—as; āśayāt—from their source (flowers).
verses.translation: When the master of the bodily vehicle (the Jiva) obtains a new body or departs from the old one, he carries these senses and the mind along with him, just as the wind carries aromas from their source.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna provides a graphic insight into the transmigration of the soul (Reincarnation). Just as the breeze wafts sweet perfumes from blossoming gardens, the departing subtle body carries the impressions of the senses and mind to the next physical womb.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna provides a graphic insight into the transmigration of the soul (Reincarnation). Just as the breeze wafts sweet perfumes from blossoming gardens, the departing subtle body carries the impressions of the senses and mind to the next physical womb.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
श्रोत्रं चक्षुः स्पर्शनं च रसनं घ्राणमेव च |
अधिष्ठाय मनश्चायं विषयानुपसेवते || ९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
श्रोत्रं चक्षुः स्पर्शनं च रसनं घ्राणमेव च |
अधिष्ठाय मनश्चायं विषयानुपसेवते || ९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
śrotraṃ cakṣuḥ sparśanaṃ ca rasanaṃ ghrāṇameva ca |
adhiṣṭhāya manaścāyaṃ viṣayānupasevate || 9 ||
verses.word_meanings: śrotram—the ear (hearing); cakṣuḥ—the eye (sight); sparśanam—the sense of touch; ca—and; rasanam—the tongue (taste); ghrāṇam—the nose (smell); eva ca—and also; adhiṣṭhāya—presiding over; manaḥ ca—and the mind; ayam—this (embodied soul); viṣayān—sense objects; upasevate—experiences/enjoys.
verses.translation: Presiding over the ear, the eye, the sense of touch, the tongue, the nose, and the mind, this embodied soul experiences the objects of the senses.
verses.meaning: The physical organs are merely instruments; the real experiencer is the conscious soul operating through the subtle cognitive apparatus of the mind and five perceptual senses.
verses.purport: The physical organs are merely instruments; the real experiencer is the conscious soul operating through the subtle cognitive apparatus of the mind and five perceptual senses.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
उत्क्रामन्तं स्थितं वापि भुञ्जानं वा गुणान्वितम् |
विमूढा नानुपश्यन्ति पश्यन्ति ज्ञानचक्षुषः || १० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
उत्क्रामन्तं स्थितं वापि भुञ्जानं वा गुणान्वितम् |
विमूढा नानुपश्यन्ति पश्यन्ति ज्ञानचक्षुषः || १० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
utkrāmantaṃ sthitaṃ vāpi bhuñjānaṃ vā guṇānvitam |
vimūḍhā nānupaśyanti paśyanti jñānacakṣuṣaḥ || 10 ||
verses.word_meanings: utkrāmantam—departing from the body; sthitam—abiding in the body; vā api—or even; bhuñjānam—experiencing; vā—or; guṇa-anvitam—endowed with the gunas; vimūḍhāḥ—the deluded; na anupaśyanti—do not perceive; paśyanti—perceive; jñāna-cakṣuṣaḥ—those endowed with the eye of wisdom.
verses.translation: The deluded do not perceive the soul when it departs from the body, when it abides within it, or when it experiences sense objects under the influence of the gunas. But those endowed with the eye of wisdom (Jnana-chakshus) perceive It clearly.
verses.meaning: Materialistic observers see only the biological organism eating, sleeping, and dying. But the enlightened seer possesses the 'Eye of Wisdom' and recognizes the distinct, immortal conscious witness inhabiting and transcending the physical frame.
verses.purport: Materialistic observers see only the biological organism eating, sleeping, and dying. But the enlightened seer possesses the 'Eye of Wisdom' and recognizes the distinct, immortal conscious witness inhabiting and transcending the physical frame.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यतन्तो योगिनश्चैनं पश्यन्त्यात्मन्यवस्थितम् |
यतन्तोऽप्यकृतात्मानो नैनं पश्यन्त्यचेतसः || ११ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यतन्तो योगिनश्चैनं पश्यन्त्यात्मन्यवस्थितम् |
यतन्तोऽप्यकृतात्मानो नैनं पश्यन्त्यचेतसः || ११ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yatanto yoginaścainaṃ paśyantyātmanyavasthitam |
yatanto'pyakṛtātmāno nainaṃ paśyantyacetasaḥ || 11 ||
verses.word_meanings: yatantaḥ—striving/endeavoring; yoginaḥ—the yogis; ca—and; enam—this Self; paśyanti—perceive/behold; ātmani avasthitam—situated within their own heart/Self; yatantaḥ api—even though striving; akṛta-ātmānaḥ—those of unpurified mind; na—not; enam—this Self; paśyanti—perceive; acetasaḥ—lacking discernment/wisdom.
verses.translation: The striving yogis perceive this Self situated within their own hearts; but the unpurified and undisciplined, even though striving, cannot perceive It, lacking inner discernment.
verses.meaning: Intellectual study alone is insufficient to realize God. Without inner purity (Chitta-shuddhi), self-control, and meditation, the divine indweller remains veiled.
verses.purport: Intellectual study alone is insufficient to realize God. Without inner purity (Chitta-shuddhi), self-control, and meditation, the divine indweller remains veiled.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यदादित्यगतं तेजो जगद्भासयतेऽखिलम् |
यच्चन्द्रमसि यच्चाग्नौ तत्तेजो विद्धि मामकम् || १२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यदादित्यगतं तेजो जगद्भासयतेऽखिलम् |
यच्चन्द्रमसि यच्चाग्नौ तत्तेजो विद्धि मामकम् || १२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yadādityagataṃ tejo jagadbhāsayate'khilam |
yaccandramasi yaccāgnau tattejo viddhi māmakam || 12 ||
verses.word_meanings: yat—which; āditya-gatam—situated in the sun; tejaḥ—radiance/effulgence; jagat—the universe; bhāsayate—illuminates; akhilam—entire; yat candramasi—which is in the moon; yat ca agnau—and which is in fire; tat—that; tejaḥ—radiance/splendor; viddhi—know; māmakam—to be Mine.
verses.translation: That dazzling radiance in the sun which illumines the entire universe, that which is in the moon, and that which is in fire—know all that splendor to be Mine.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna reveals Himself as the cosmic powerhouse: All solar thermonuclear energy, the soothing lunar luminescence, and terrestrial fire derive their foundational luminance from the Supreme Lord's infinite effulgence.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna reveals Himself as the cosmic powerhouse: All solar thermonuclear energy, the soothing lunar luminescence, and terrestrial fire derive their foundational luminance from the Supreme Lord's infinite effulgence.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
गामाविश्य च भूतानि धारयाम्यहमोजसा |
पुष्णामि चौषधीः सर्वाः सोमो भूत्वा रसात्मकः || १३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
गामाविश्य च भूतानि धारयाम्यहमोजसा |
पुष्णामि चौषधीः सर्वाः सोमो भूत्वा रसात्मकः || १३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
gāmāviśya ca bhūtāni dhārayāmyahamojasā |
puṣṇāmi cauṣadhīḥ sarvāḥ somo bhūtvā rasātmakaḥ || 13 ||
verses.word_meanings: gām—the earth/planets; āviśya—entering/permeating; ca—and; bhūtāni—all living beings; dhārayāmi—I sustain/support; aham—I; ojasā—by My vital cosmic energy/gravity; puṣṇāmi—I nourish; ca—and; auṣadhīḥ—herbs and plant life; sarvāḥ—all; somaḥ—the moon; bhūtvā—becoming; rasa-ātmakaḥ—the source of nectar/sap.
verses.translation: Permeating the earth, I sustain all living beings by My vital cosmic energy; and becoming the nectar-bearing moon (Soma), I nourish all herbs, vegetables, and plant life.
verses.meaning: The Lord maintains orbital planetary stability (gravitational energy / Ojas) and bestows life-giving nutritional potency to agricultural crops and medicinal flora through the lunar rays.
verses.purport: The Lord maintains orbital planetary stability (gravitational energy / Ojas) and bestows life-giving nutritional potency to agricultural crops and medicinal flora through the lunar rays.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अहं वैश्वानरो भूत्वा प्राणिनां देहमाश्रितः |
प्राणापानसमायुक्तः पचाम्यन्नं चतुर्विधम् || १४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अहं वैश्वानरो भूत्वा प्राणिनां देहमाश्रितः |
प्राणापानसमायुक्तः पचाम्यन्नं चतुर्विधम् || १४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
ahaṃ vaiśvānaro bhūtvā prāṇināṃ dehamāśritaḥ |
prāṇāpānasamāyuktaḥ pacāmyannaṃ caturvidham || 14 ||
verses.word_meanings: aham—I; vaiśvānaraḥ—the digestive fire (Vaishvanara / Jatharagni); bhūtvā—becoming; prāṇinām—of all living entities; deham—the body; āśritaḥ—abiding within; prāṇa-apāna-samāyuktaḥ—united with incoming (Prana) and outgoing (Apana) vital breaths; pacāmi—I digest; annam—food; catur-vidham—the four types (chewed, sucked, licked, and drunk).
verses.translation: Becoming the digestive fire (Vaishvanara) abiding within the bodies of all living creatures, and united with the vital breaths of Prana and Apana, I digest the four kinds of food.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna sustains physical life from within: As the internal metabolic digestive energy (Vaishvanara / Jatharagni), He breaks down all four varieties of human sustenance—chewed (Bhakshya), drunk (Peya), licked (Lehya), and sucked (Choshya)—transforming food into life energy.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna sustains physical life from within: As the internal metabolic digestive energy (Vaishvanara / Jatharagni), He breaks down all four varieties of human sustenance—chewed (Bhakshya), drunk (Peya), licked (Lehya), and sucked (Choshya)—transforming food into life energy.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सर्वस्य चाहं हृदि सन्निविष्टो मत्तः स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनं च |
वेदैश्च सर्वैरहमेव वेद्यो वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव चाहम् || १५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सर्वस्य चाहं हृदि सन्निविष्टो मत्तः स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनं च |
वेदैश्च सर्वैरहमेव वेद्यो वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव चाहम् || १५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
sarvasya cāhaṃ hṛdi sanniviṣṭo mattaḥ smṛtirjñānamapohanaṃ ca |
vedaiśca sarvairahameva vedyo vedāntakṛdvedavideva cāham || 15 ||
verses.word_meanings: sarvasya—of all living beings; ca—and; aham—I; hṛdi—in the heart; sanniviṣṭaḥ—seated as the indwelling witness (Antaryamin); mattaḥ—from Me; smṛtiḥ—memory; jñānam—knowledge/perception; apohanam—loss of memory / oblivion; ca—and; vedaiḥ—by the Vedas; ca—and; sarvaiḥ—all; aham—I; eva—alone; vedyaḥ—to be known; vedānta-kṛt—the author of the Vedanta; veda-vit—the knower of the Vedas; eva ca—and also; aham—I.
verses.translation: And I am seated within the hearts of all living beings; from Me come memory, knowledge, and their loss. By all the Vedas, I alone am to be known; I am indeed the author of the Vedanta and the supreme Knower of the Vedas.
verses.meaning: This pivotal verse is one of the grandest summits of the Gita. Sri Krishna is the Antaryamin (indwelling Paramatman) orchestrating human cognition and memory. All scriptural revelation points exclusively to Him as the ultimate truth to be known (Vedya), the composer of Vedanta (through Vyasa), and the master knower of all Vedic wisdom.
verses.purport: This pivotal verse is one of the grandest summits of the Gita. Sri Krishna is the Antaryamin (indwelling Paramatman) orchestrating human cognition and memory. All scriptural revelation points exclusively to Him as the ultimate truth to be known (Vedya), the composer of Vedanta (through Vyasa), and the master knower of all Vedic wisdom.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च |
क्षरः सर्वाणि भूतानि कूटस्थोऽक्षर उच्यते || १६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च |
क्षरः सर्वाणि भूतानि कूटस्थोऽक्षर उच्यते || १६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
dvāvimau puruṣau loke kṣaraścākṣara eva ca |
kṣaraḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni kūṭastho'kṣara ucyate || 16 ||
verses.word_meanings: dvau—two; imau—these; puruṣau—categories of beings; loke—in the cosmos; kṣaraḥ—the perishable; ca—and; akṣaraḥ—the imperishable; eva ca—and also; kṣaraḥ—the perishable; sarvāṇi bhūtāni—all changing material bodies/creatures; kūṭa-sthaḥ—the changeless/immutable soul; akṣaraḥ—imperishable; ucyate—is called.
verses.translation: There are two orders of beings in this world: the Perishable (Kshara) and the Imperishable (Akshara). All physical bodies are the perishable, while the changeless conscious soul is called the imperishable.
verses.meaning: Verses 16, 17, and 18 form the famous 'Tri-shloki Gita' (the three-verse essence of Vedic metaphysics). First, Sri Krishna delineates Kshara (all changing material forms subject to decay) and Akshara (the unmoving, changeless spiritual consciousness).
verses.purport: Verses 16, 17, and 18 form the famous 'Tri-shloki Gita' (the three-verse essence of Vedic metaphysics). First, Sri Krishna delineates Kshara (all changing material forms subject to decay) and Akshara (the unmoving, changeless spiritual consciousness).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
उत्तमः पुरुषस्त्वन्यः परमात्मेत्युदाहृतः |
यो लोकत्रयमाविश्य बिभर्त्यव्यय ईश्वरः || १७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
उत्तमः पुरुषस्त्वन्यः परमात्मेत्युदाहृतः |
यो लोकत्रयमाविश्य बिभर्त्यव्यय ईश्वरः || १७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
uttamaḥ puruṣastvanyaḥ paramātmetyudāhṛtaḥ |
yo lokatrayamāviśya bibhartyavyaya īśvaraḥ || 17 ||
verses.word_meanings: uttamaḥ puruṣaḥ—the Supreme Person; tu—but; anyaḥ—distinct/other; parama-ātmā—the Supreme Self; iti—thus; udāhṛtaḥ—is declared; yaḥ—who; loka-trayam—the three cosmic worlds; āviśya—pervading/entering; bibharti—sustains/maintains; avyayaḥ—the imperishable; īśvaraḥ—the Supreme Sovereign Lord.
verses.translation: Distinct from both of these is the Supreme Divine Person (Uttama Purusha), designated as the Paramatman (Supreme Self), who, pervading the three cosmic realms, sustains them as the eternal, immutable Sovereign Lord.
verses.meaning: The second verse of the Tri-shloki Gita unveils the third and highest category: 'Uttama Purusha' (Paramatman / Bhagavan). He is distinct from both perishable matter (Kshara) and individual liberated souls (Akshara), sustaining the entire universe through His omnipotent grace.
verses.purport: The second verse of the Tri-shloki Gita unveils the third and highest category: 'Uttama Purusha' (Paramatman / Bhagavan). He is distinct from both perishable matter (Kshara) and individual liberated souls (Akshara), sustaining the entire universe through His omnipotent grace.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यस्मात्क्षरमतीतोऽहमक्षरादपि चोत्तमः |
अतोऽस्मि लोके वेदे च प्रथितः पुरुषोत्तमः || १८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यस्मात्क्षरमतीतोऽहमक्षरादपि चोत्तमः |
अतोऽस्मि लोके वेदे च प्रथितः पुरुषोत्तमः || १८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yasmātkṣaramatīto'hamakṣarādapi cottamaḥ |
ato'smi loke vede ca prathitaḥ puruṣottamaḥ || 18 ||
verses.word_meanings: yasmāt—because; kṣaram—the perishable matter; atītaḥ—transcendental to; aham—I; akṣarāt—than the imperishable soul; api—even; ca—and; uttamaḥ—supreme/higher; ataḥ—therefore; asmi—I am; loke—in the world; vede—in the Vedas; ca—and; prathitaḥ—celebrated/renowned; puruṣa-uttamaḥ—as Purushottama (the Supreme Person).
verses.translation: Because I transcend the perishable (Kshara) and am superior even to the imperishable (Akshara), I am celebrated both in the world and in the Vedas as Purushottama (the Supreme Divine Person).
verses.meaning: The grand culmination of the Tri-shloki Gita: Sri Krishna explicitly identifies Himself as Purushottama—the Supreme Transcendence above material nature and higher even than individual spirit. This is the supreme theological crest-jewel of the Bhagavad Gita.
verses.purport: The grand culmination of the Tri-shloki Gita: Sri Krishna explicitly identifies Himself as Purushottama—the Supreme Transcendence above material nature and higher even than individual spirit. This is the supreme theological crest-jewel of the Bhagavad Gita.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यो मामेवमसम्मूढो जानाति पुरुषोत्तमम् |
स सर्वविद्भजति मां सर्वभावेन भारत || १९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यो मामेवमसम्मूढो जानाति पुरुषोत्तमम् |
स सर्वविद्भजति मां सर्वभावेन भारत || १९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yo māmevamasammūḍho jānāti puruṣottamam |
sa sarvavidbhajati māṃ sarvabhāvena bhārata || 19 ||
verses.word_meanings: yaḥ—whoever; mām—Me; evam—thus; asammūḍhaḥ—undeluded; jānāti—knows; puruṣa-uttamam—as the Supreme Person; saḥ—he; sarva-vit—knower of all (all-knowing); bhajati—worships/adores; mām—Me; sarva-bhāvena—with his whole being and all his heart; bhārata—O descendant of Bharata (Arjuna).
verses.translation: He who, free from delusion, thus knows Me as the Supreme Divine Person (Purushottama), knows everything that is to be known, O Bharata, and worships Me with his whole being.
verses.meaning: To realize Sri Krishna as Purushottama is the synthesis of all knowledge (Sarva-vit). It naturally culminates in total, unalloyed loving surrender (Sarva-bhavena Bhakti).
verses.purport: To realize Sri Krishna as Purushottama is the synthesis of all knowledge (Sarva-vit). It naturally culminates in total, unalloyed loving surrender (Sarva-bhavena Bhakti).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
इति गुह्यतमं शास्त्रमिदमुक्तं मयानघ |
एतद्बुद्ध्वा बुद्धिमान्स्यात्कृतकृत्यश्च भारत || २० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
इति गुह्यतमं शास्त्रमिदमुक्तं मयानघ |
एतद्बुद्ध्वा बुद्धिमान्स्यात्कृतकृत्यश्च भारत || २० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
iti guhyatamaṃ śāstramidamuktaṃ mayānagha |
etadbuddhvā buddhimānsyātkṛtakṛtyaśca bhārata || 20 ||
verses.word_meanings: iti—thus; guhya-tamam—the most confidential/secret; śāstram—sacred scripture/doctrine; idam—this; uktam—has been revealed; mayā—by Me; anagha—O sinless one (Arjuna); etat—this; buddhvā—understanding; buddhimān—truly enlightened/wise; syāt—one becomes; kṛta-kṛtyaḥ—fulfilled in all duties / having accomplished life's purpose; ca—and; bhārata—O descendant of Bharata.
verses.translation: Thus, O sinless one, this most confidential sacred science (Guhyatama Shastra) has been revealed by Me. By understanding this, a seeker becomes truly enlightened and attains the ultimate fulfillment of life's purpose (Krita-kritya), O Bharata.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna seals Chapter 15 with this benediction: The doctrine of Purushottama is the deepest mystery of all Vedic wisdom. One who realizes this truth achieves the highest spiritual enlightenment and attains 'Krita-krityata'—the supreme state of having fulfilled every human and spiritual obligation.
verses.purport: Sri Krishna seals Chapter 15 with this benediction: The doctrine of Purushottama is the deepest mystery of all Vedic wisdom. One who realizes this truth achieves the highest spiritual enlightenment and attains 'Krita-krityata'—the supreme state of having fulfilled every human and spiritual obligation.
